title: Engine Error Feedback Into Context
scope: How TurnEngine feeds ALL tool execution errors back into the LLM conversation history so the model can self-correct inline — the core anti-hallucination pattern.

error_feedback_mechanism.behavior: Catches ALL exceptions from tool execution and returns {"error": str(exc), "error_type": type(exc).__name__} as a tuple (result, status). No exception escapes to crash the turn.
error_feedback_mechanism.context_injection: _record_result (engine.py:789) calls _tool_result_message(tool_call, result) which appends a role='tool' message with json.dumps(result) content + tool_call_id to self.messages — the LLM SEES the error in its next turn's conversation history.
error_feedback_mechanism.contrast: ai-factory defers verification to post-run ruff/pyright — the LLM never sees its own tool execution failures in context, so it cannot self-correct. output_sanitizer.py only repairs broken JSON offline.

no_silent_failures.interrupted_tools: _interrupted_tool (engine.py:651) appends _tool_error_message with 'interrupted by user' reason — no orphaned tool_calls
no_silent_failures.denied_tools: _authorize (engine.py:757) appends _tool_error_message for denied/unknown tool calls — LLM sees why a tool was rejected
no_silent_failures.audit_sink: _audit (engine.py:837) fires an audit_sink callback with full context (tool_name, arguments, stage, status, result_preview) — structured observability side-channel

message_format.preview: _preview (engine.py:1189) — truncates result to 300 chars in audit events for readable observability

tool_registry_structure.storage: dict[str, ToolSpec] — name to (schema, func, metadata) mapping
tool_registry_structure.registration: register(func, metadata=None, schema=None) — extracts name from __name__, schema via _schema_for() using aisuite Tools
tool_registry_structure.execute: execute(name, arguments) — looks up ToolSpec, calls spec.func(**arguments); raises KeyError for unknown tools
tool_registry_structure.unknown_tool_handling: engine.py:758-759 — if spec is None (unknown tool), reason='unknown tool: {name}', error message appended to history, TOOL_FINISHED with status='denied'

guard_toolset_callsite.delegation_point: self.wrapped.call_tool(name, tool_args, ctx, tool) at line 260 — bare delegation with NO try/except, NO error envelope injection
guard_toolset_callsite.agent_construction: factory/infra/tools_skill.py:301 — Agent(output_type=..., retries=5, toolsets=[guard_tools(...)]) — already has retry budget but tool exceptions propagate as unstructured tracebacks
guard_toolset_callsite.consequence: When a tool fails (file not found, syntax error, permission denied), the exception kills the agent run or gets swallowed — the LLM never sees the error in its conversation history and cannot self-correct

pydantic_ai_retry_mech.mech: ModelRetry (pydantic_ai.exceptions) — raised from within a tool function, Pydantic-AI catches it and adds a RetryPromptPart to the message history, then re-sends the request
pydantic_ai_retry_mech.retries_param: Agent(retries=5) at tools_skill.py:301 — framework-managed retry budget, but only triggers on ModelRetry (not generic exceptions)
pydantic_ai_retry_mech.tool_error_propagation: When self.wrapped.call_tool() at tools_guard.py:260 raises a non-ModelRetry exception, it propagates up through Pydantic-AI's ToolExecutionError path — the error is NOT injected into conversation history as a retry prompt
pydantic_ai_retry_mech.fix: Wrap call_tool delegation in try/except, catch Exception, raise ToolError(envelope.model_dump_json()) where ToolError subclasses ModelRetry

post_run_verification_gap.current: ai-factory runs ruff + pyright + CC checks AFTER the agent run completes (factory/infra/validation.py) — all verification is deferred, the LLM never sees failures in-turn
post_run_verification_gap.openworker: Verification is INLINE — _record_result appends the error to self.messages before the next iteration, so the LLM learns from its mistake immediately
post_run_verification_gap.impact: Deferred verification means the LLM repeats the same hallucinated tool call across multiple retry cycles, wasting API calls and producing garbage output

proposal: ai-factory's tools_guard.py / GuardToolset must intercept EVERY tool call result and inject errors back into the agent's conversation history as tool messages before returning. Currently, when a tool fails (file not found, syntax error, permission denied), the error surfaces only in deferred ruff/verifier output AFTER the LLM stops — the LLM never learns it made a bad call. Adopting openworker's _execute_sync pattern means wrapping every tool call in try/except, returning {"error": str(exc), "error_type": type(exc).__name__} as a tool message, and raising ModelRetry so the LLM sees the failure and self-corrects inline. This is the single highest-impact fix for hallucination-driven garbage output.

pydantic_ai_2_impl.pattern: ToolError (subclass of ModelRetry) + ToolErrorEnvelope (output_type BaseModel) at the GuardToolset.tool boundary — every tool failure becomes a visible retry prompt in the LLM conversation, triggering automatic self-correction.
pydantic_ai_2_impl.code:
import json
from pydantic import BaseModel
from pydantic_ai.exceptions import ModelRetry


class ToolError(ModelRetry):
    """Surface tool failures as visible retry messages in LLM conversation.

    Subclasses ModelRetry so Pydantic-AI injects the error as a retry prompt
    part in the conversation history — the LLM sees the failure and self-corrects.
    """


class ToolErrorEnvelope(BaseModel):
    tool_name: str
    error: str
    error_type: str
    reason: str | None = None


# Agent construction (factory/infra/tools_skill.py:301) already uses
# output_type + retries=5 for typed validation and retry budget:
#   agent = Agent(
#       model=model,
#       toolsets=[guard_tools(resolved_tools, budget)],
#       output_type=output_type,  # e.g. TaskResult pydantic model
#       retries=5,
#       model_settings=ModelSettings(parallel_tool_calls=False),
#   )
#
# INJECTION POINT — factory/infra/tools_guard.py:260, GuardToolset.call_tool:
#
#   CURRENT (broken — bare delegation, errors kill the turn):
#     result = await self.wrapped.call_tool(name, tool_args, ctx, tool)
#
#   ENRICHED — wrap in try/except, raise ToolError so Pydantic-AI injects
#   the failure as a visible retry prompt in conversation history:
try:
    result = await self.wrapped.call_tool(name, tool_args, ctx, tool)
except Exception as exc:
    envelope = ToolErrorEnvelope(
        tool_name=name,
        error=str(exc),
        error_type=type(exc).__name__,
        reason="tool execution failed — see error_type for details",
    )
    raise ToolError(envelope.model_dump_json())  # visible retry prompt triggers ModelRetry self-correction
pydantic_ai_2_impl.why_now: ai-factory's LLMs keep producing hallucinated tool calls (wrong file paths, nonexistent commands, invalid arguments) because they never see the failure. OpenWorker's _execute_sync (engine.py:782) proves that feeding structured {"error", "error_type"} back as a tool message closes the self-correction loop — the model learns from its mistake in-turn instead of repeating it across retries. Pydantic-AI 2.0's ModelRetry mechanism is designed exactly for this: raise it from a tool boundary and the framework injects a retry prompt into the conversation. ai-factory already has retries=5 at tools_skill.py:301 but tool exceptions bypass it because they're not ModelRetry.
pydantic_ai_2_impl.harness_gap: factory/infra/tools_guard.py:260 — GuardToolset.call_tool delegates to self.wrapped.call_tool(name, tool_args, ctx, tool) without a try/except wrapper. Tool exceptions propagate as unstructured tracebacks (ToolExecutionError) that kill the run or get swallowed silently — no {"error": ..., "error_type": ...} envelope is injected into the conversation history. Fix: wrap line 260 in try/except Exception, construct a ToolErrorEnvelope(tool_name, error, error_type, reason) via Pydantic model_dump_json(), and raise ToolError(...) (a subclass of ModelRetry) so Pydantic-AI injects the failure as a visible retry prompt at line 152-271 of tools_guard.py, with the Agent's retries=5 budget (tools_skill.py:301) handling the retry loop.

implementation_notes: Key findings for implementation: (1) GuardToolset.call_tool at tools_guard.py:152 is the single chokepoint — ALL agent tool calls route through it. (2) The bare delegation at line 260 must be wrapped in try/except Exception. (3) ToolError must subclass ModelRetry (from pydantic_ai.exceptions) since pydantic_ai does not export ToolError directly in v2.14.1. (4) ToolErrorEnvelope is a Pydantic BaseModel whose model_dump_json() becomes the ModelRetry.message visible to the LLM. (5) The existing retries=5 at tools_skill.py:301 already caps retry attempts; the error feedback just makes each retry informed. (6) Failed calls should NOT increment self._used budget — the LLM should retry without penalty. (7) The _seen cache at line 262 should not cache error results — raise ToolError before reaching the cache block.
